atoms.b: My name is ((++Galileo_Galilei Dmitrii_Mendeleev)) and I was an Italian scientist working in the ((++16th_and_17th_centuries 21st_century)).
My most famous ((++discovery recipe)) about gravity involved dropping objects of different ((++masses tastes)) off the Leaning Tower of Pisa.
I proved that the ((++speed colour)) of an object ((++falling rising)) is not linked to its mass, meaning that ((++gravity friction)) pulls all objects equally.

As this happened so long ago, no one knows whether I actually conducted this test or whether it was just a ((++thought_experiment dream)). Either way, my discovery disproved an idea that people had held since Aristotle and the ancient ((++Greeks Dutch))!

atoms.text: Abigail has come to Pisa to recreate Galileo’s experiment and confirm his results.
She climbs to the top of the tower with three spheres of different masses to see how long it takes for each of them to reach the ground.

atoms.a: What must Abigail ensure stays consistent in her experiment to achieve accurate results?
b: ++the height the spheres are dropped from

feedback.finish: The height that Abigail drops the spheres from must remain constant to ensure that only the effect of the spheres’ mass on gravity is being tested.

instruction.text: Watch Abigail drop the spheres from the Leaning Tower of Pisa and see what happens.

atoms.a: Did the mass of the spheres affect how quickly they fell?
Did the result of Abigail’s experiment match that of Galileo?
